title: scratch.open refuses any program whose name does not start with decade-
body:
`scratch.open` starts a program in the workspace's scratch pane. Before it starts anything, `check_program` in `src/server/scratch.rs` refuses a program whose name does not start with `decade-` or that contains a `/`. Then it checks that the program is an executable file on decade's `PATH`. An agent asked to open `acre-gui` got this error:

```text
acre-gui is not a bare program name starting with decade-
```

The prefix came from `decade-c62fae`. It was chosen to match how decade-apps names its binaries, as an alternative to a config list of allowed programs. Jack never meant it as a rule. It keeps out every program not built for decade and protects nothing, because the person already chose the scratch pane and the agent can run any program from its own shell.

## Proposal

- `check_program` drops both the prefix rule and the bare-name rule.
- A name with a `/` in it is a path, resolved against the workspace directory, so `./target/debug/acre-gui` works for relaunching a fresh build. A name without one is looked up on decade's `PATH`, as now.
- The check that the program exists and is executable stays, so a typo still gets a clear error before decade closes the pane's current program.
- The `scratch.open` description and the server instructions in `src/server/mcp.rs` drop the prefix, as does the `scratch.open` paragraph in `docs/protocol.md`.

## Cost

`decade` takes a `### Changed` entry under Unreleased. The change widens what a call accepts, so it breaks no caller and moves the patch.
